catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits one rosbridge publication of geometry_msgs/Twist. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a duration and reports distance and heading, while the pinned cmd_vel callback stores only linear.x, linear.y and angular.x and publishes no motion acknowledgement. A rosbridge publish receipt is transmission evidence only.
No catalogue class selects a quadruped gait. The pinned gait_type service stores an integer selector and returns a fixed result 0; it is not a joint-motion, velocity or mobile-base command class.
No catalogue class sets a controller high/low-power mode. The pinned robot_mode service stores an integer and returns result 0; it is not a stop, joint-motion or mobile-base class.

No catalogue class fits a fixed standing-gait request. cap.motion.stop.v1 requires stopped-state evidence, while the gait_type callback only acknowledges that it stored cmd=4 and does not measure quiescence. The x-cap carries the fixed request and the limitation is disclosed in safe_state and the fidelity gaps.
No catalogue class reads a nav_msgs/Odometry pose sample. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 is a bounded motion command with distance and heading output, not a topic observation.

No catalogue class fits this fixed /imu0 subscription. cap.sensing.imu.v1 requires a frame input and a sampled_at string output; the pinned sample is a raw sensor_msgs/Imu with a ROS header stamp and no caller-selected frame. The x-cap exposes the message fields without inventing a timestamp.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every endpoint, type, fact and the four sourced limits (the x and y clamps at ConvexMPCLocomotion.cpp:89-101, gait 0..11 from README.md:69-80, mode 0..1 from GaitCtrller.h:84-85; yaw rate operator_required) against the pin, then traced the declared e-stop. The e-stop and safe-state action were the /gait_type cmd=4 standing-gait request, acknowledged unconditionally by a callback that only stores the selector, and ConvexMPCLocomotion::run honours the gait type only in robot mode 0 (148-185), while the node sets robot mode 1 in __reset_robot and then enters run(), whose loop never returns, so set_robot_mode(0) is not reached (walking_simulation.py:194-198, 205): after start-up the node runs in robot mode 1, where the stop request does not stop a walking robot, yet the SDK reported the e-stop as completed. Reviewer removed the e-stop binding and safe_state=True, rewrote safe_state, the docstring, one stop gap and the stand description, added two source facts (driver.py), changed the e-stop case to expect MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held (test_driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED, as mrpt/mvsim does; the 14 package cases pass, and collect.py reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator writes status blocked. For the human reviewer: The node offers no acknowledged stop: /gait_type and /robot_mode callbacks return result 0 unconditionally after storing a value, cmd_vel is a plain subscription, and in robot mode 1 the controller ignores the gait type. A two-step stop (robot_mode 0, then gait_type 4) cannot be expressed as one fixed safety binding and would still race other ROS clients. Unblocking needs a stop the controller acknowledges, or an SDK profile for an ordered multi-service stop with a sensed standing check.
